app.setup.title_default.why: plain factual statement of current state, matching System Settings register; avoids duplicating the button below

app.setup.title_failed.why: hedged toward 'we could not tell', distinct from the plain not-on state above

app.setup.detail_default.s: Под защитой сайт больше не сможет перехватывать нажатия.
app.setup.detail_default.back: Under protection a site will no longer be able to intercept presses.
app.setup.detail_default.why: one plain sentence stating the payoff, concrete rather than a slogan

app.setup.detail_failed.s: Safari не ответил сейчас, но при включении расширения приложение заметит это само.
app.setup.detail_failed.back: Safari didn't respond now, but when the extension is turned on, the app will notice it itself.
app.setup.detail_failed.why: joined with 'но' rather than a dash; hides the raw system error and reassures no manual refresh is needed

app.setup.open_button.why: Apple's own term for the pane ('Расширения'); works verbatim on both the setup screen and the welcome sheet

app.welcome.heading.why: the one place allowed a warmer register; product name kept untranslated as a proper noun

app.welcome.feature.invisible_layers.tit.why: plain concrete noun phrase naming the trick, no marketing language

app.welcome.feature.invisible_layers.det.s: Невидимый слой может перехватить нажатие, предназначенное для другого.
app.welcome.feature.invisible_layers.det.back: An invisible layer can intercept a press meant for something else.
app.welcome.feature.invisible_layers.det.why: describes what the person would experience, not the mechanism

app.welcome.feature.swapped_links.title.why: short concrete noun phrase for the trick

app.welcome.feature.swapped_links.detail.s: Некоторые страницы меняют адрес ссылки в момент нажатия.
app.welcome.feature.swapped_links.detail.back: Some pages change the link's address at the moment of the press.
app.welcome.feature.swapped_links.detail.why: plain, concrete, describes the visible effect

app.welcome.feature.uninvited_windows.ti.why: short noun phrase naming the trick

app.welcome.feature.uninvited_windows.de.s: С защитой новая вкладка откроет только то, что вы нажали.
app.welcome.feature.uninvited_windows.de.back: With protection, the new tab will open only what you pressed.
app.welcome.feature.uninvited_windows.de.why: phrased as a promise rather than a description of the trick, as the brief asks

app.welcome.feature.every_destination.ti.why: names the rule-list feature: every address is tracked, not only the ones the guard stops

app.welcome.feature.every_destination.de.s: Каждый адрес попадает в список, где вы разрешаете или блокируете его.
app.welcome.feature.every_destination.de.back: Every address ends up in a list, where you allow or block it.
app.welcome.feature.every_destination.de.why: covers both scopes (site/everywhere) in one plain sentence without naming them explicitly, to stay under budget

app.welcome.feature.one_site_at_a_time.d.s: Кнопка Undirect на панели Safari включает защиту для этого сайта.
app.welcome.feature.one_site_at_a_time.d.back: The Undirect button on Safari's toolbar turns on protection for this site.
app.welcome.feature.one_site_at_a_time.d.why: names the actual mechanism (the toolbar button), concrete rather than abstract

app.nav.guarded_sites.why: vocabulary term for 'guarded site'; short enough for both a sidebar row and a nav title

app.nav.settings.why: Apple's own term for this screen on iOS and macOS

app.nav.app_title.why: proper noun, left untranslated like any other app's own name

app.rules.grouping.everywhere.why: one word, reused consistently for the 'everywhere' scope concept across the product

app.rules.grouping.by_site.why: clear opposite of 'Везде' when the two sit side by side

app.rules.empty_no_app.title.why: names the wiring/first-contact state, distinct from 'no rules exist yet'

app.rules.empty_no_app.detail.s: Откройте страницу в Safari, и список заполнится сам.
app.rules.empty_no_app.detail.back: Open a page in Safari, and the list will fill itself.
app.rules.empty_no_app.detail.why: states the simple fix, no setting to change

app.rules.empty_no_rules.title.why: contrasts with the first-contact empty state above: the app is connected, this list is just empty

app.rules.empty_no_rules.detail.s: Правило появится здесь, когда вы примете решение.
app.rules.empty_no_rules.detail.back: A rule will appear here once you make a decision.
app.rules.empty_no_rules.detail.why: explains a rule is created only by an explicit decision, not merely by the guard seeing something

app.rules.footer.lifetime_count.why: shown here is the 'many' plural form; Russian needs three forms for %lld — one: '%lld попытка заблокирована', few (2-4): '%lld попытки заблокированы', many (0, 5+): '%lld попытки заблокировано' — implement via a stringsdict with those three keys rather than a single string

app.rules.row.state_blocked.why: impersonal passive, pairs cleanly as the opposite of 'Разрешено'

app.rules.row.action_allow.why: infinitive verb, Apple's convention for a menu action, distinct from the adjective form used for the current state

app.rules.row.action_block.why: infinitive verb, only shown when the row is currently Allowed

app.rules.row.help_tooltip.why: describes what the hovered control does, using the same verbs as the menu items it governs

app.rules.row.use_default.why: names clearing the explicit rule so the destination falls back to the default policy, not a new verdict

app.watched.empty.title.why: plain statement that no site has been switched on yet

app.watched.empty.detail.s: Нажмите Undirect на панели Safari, когда сайт начинает мешать.
app.watched.empty.detail.back: Press Undirect on Safari's toolbar when a site starts to bother you.
app.watched.empty.detail.why: tells the person exactly how to guard their first site

app.watched.footer.s: Новые сайты добавляются только кнопкой в Safari.
app.watched.footer.back: New sites are added only through the button in Safari.
app.watched.footer.why: reminds this screen has no way to add a site itself

app.watched.row.guarded_badge.why: read-only status word, purely informational on iOS

app.watched.row.stop_button.why: short imperative verb suitable for a small trailing row button

app.watched.row.stop_tooltip.back: Turns off protection for this site
app.watched.row.stop_tooltip.why: describes what the Stop button under the pointer does

app.settings.guard_toggle.why: the vocabulary noun for 'guard', kept consistent as the label of the master switch

app.settings.state_on.why: generic neuter form, reused for more than one setting on this screen

app.settings.state_off.why: clear opposite of state_on, equally generic

app.settings.mode_heading.why: introduces the choice between watched-only and every-site running

app.settings.mode_watched.why: described from the person's own point of view, the default conservative choice

app.settings.mode_everywhere.why: reused consistently with the other 'everywhere' scope labels in the product

app.settings.banner_toggle.why: vocabulary term for the on-page banner, separate from the popup's own record

app.settings.policy_heading.why: introduces the choice for an unrated destination; kept short rather than padded to hit a word count

app.settings.policy_block.why: imperfective infinitive describing an ongoing default policy, not a one-off action

app.settings.policy_allow.why: imperfective infinitive, paired in aspect with 'Блокировать'

ext.meta.name.why: proper noun, the extension's own listed name

ext.meta.description.s: Undirect не даёт страницам открывать или перенаправлять по клику не туда, куда вы хотели.
ext.meta.description.back: Undirect doesn't let pages open or redirect by click somewhere other than where you wanted.
ext.meta.description.why: one sentence for someone who has never used the extension, slightly more explanatory than in-app copy

ext.meta.app_title.why: fallback display name, the product's own name

ext.toolbar.tooltip_on.why: states guarding is currently on for the active tab

ext.toolbar.tooltip_off.back: Protection off, press to turn on
ext.toolbar.tooltip_off.why: tooltip doubles as the call to action, since pressing the icon is how guarding starts

ext.toolbar.tooltip_no_site.why: brief: same underlying string as ext.popup.no_site_title, so phrased identically there

ext.popup.no_site_title.why: brief notes this shares its underlying string with ext.toolbar.tooltip_no_site; kept identical

ext.popup.no_site_body.s: Откройте сайт и нажмите сюда для защиты.
ext.popup.no_site_body.back: Open a site and press here for protection.
ext.popup.no_site_body.why: 'сюда' keeps the self-reference to the toolbar button the popup hangs off, rather than translating 'here' as a place

ext.popup.watch_switch_label.back: Switch of protection for this site
ext.popup.watch_switch_label.why: screen-reader-only label naming what the switch controls, since the visible row already shows the site name

ext.popup.watch_unknown.why: explains the disabled switch: no actual page here to guard

ext.popup.watch_everywhere_mode.s: Защита уже включена для всех сайтов.
ext.popup.watch_everywhere_mode.back: Protection is already on for all sites.
ext.popup.watch_everywhere_mode.why: explains the switch is redundant because 'everywhere' mode is already set in Settings

ext.popup.watch_master_off.why: explains the switch is disabled because of the master toggle, not this particular site

ext.popup.watch_on.back: Protection is on, turning it off will reload the page.
ext.popup.watch_on.why: confirms current state and warns of the reload; shares sentence shape with watch_off

ext.popup.watch_off.back: Protection is off, turning it on will reload the page.
ext.popup.watch_off.why: direct before/after counterpart to watch_on, same sentence shape

ext.popup.page_heading.why: heads the list of what the current tab specifically has reached for

ext.popup.page_off.s: Защита здесь выключена, поэтому ничего не отслеживается.
ext.popup.page_off.back: Protection is off here, so nothing is being tracked.
ext.popup.page_off.why: dead key as of 2026-09-22 (no code reads it); written speculatively to match the voice of the other page-section states, per the brief's own note

ext.popup.page_quiet.s: Эта страница пока ничего не запрашивала.
ext.popup.page_quiet.back: This page hasn't requested anything yet.
ext.popup.page_quiet.why: plain statement that nothing has tried to reach outside this page so far

ext.popup.page_empty.back: The list is empty for now.
ext.popup.page_empty.why: dead key as of 2026-09-22; per the brief's note, treated as a near-synonym of page_quiet, worded around the empty list rather than a quiet page

ext.popup.stopped_one.why: the impersonal passive 'Заблокировано' does not inflect by number, sidestepping the one/few/many mismatch since the source code only branches on 'one' vs 'other' but Russian needs three forms

ext.popup.stopped_other.why: same invariant construction as stopped_one, for the same reason — see its note

ext.popup.seen_one.why: the fixed 'Всего X:' label pattern uses a genitive-plural noun that does not change with the count, again sidestepping the two-bucket source's inability to express Russian's three plural forms

ext.popup.seen_other.why: same invariant construction as seen_one — see its note

ext.popup.tries_one.why: 'раз' shares its form between the one-count and the many-count case; the 2-4 case grammatically wants 'раза', but the two-bucket source can't express three forms, so this stays terse at a small cost of precision for that range

ext.popup.tries_other.why: same fragment and tradeoff as tries_one — see its note

ext.popup.recipe_heading.why: one-word lead-in fragment, reads naturally before 'Исправление: <текст>' when concatenated in code

ext.state.blocked.why: kept identical to app.rules.row.state_blocked so the two read the same to a user moving between surfaces; combines with a following scope word

ext.state.allowed.why: kept identical to app.rules.row.state_allowed; combines with a following scope word

ext.state.removed.why: neuter impersonal form for a row with no destination to allow or block, since a trap was simply taken off the page

ext.scope.here.why: follows a verdict word without reordering, e.g. 'Заблокировано' + 'на этом сайте'

ext.scope.everywhere.why: follows a verdict word, e.g. 'Заблокировано везде'; reuses the same word as the everywhere-scope concept elsewhere

ext.scope.default.why: follows a verdict word, e.g. 'Заблокировано по умолчанию'

ext.action.allow_here.why: menu option scoped to the current site, distinct from the everywhere variant

ext.action.allow_everywhere.why: menu option scoped to every guarded site

ext.action.block_here.why: menu option scoped to the current site

ext.action.block_everywhere.why: menu option scoped to every guarded site

ext.popup.policy_heading.why: same concept as the app's settings screen equivalent, kept identical in wording

ext.popup.bridge_warning.s: Настройки безопасности этой страницы блокируют часть защиты Undirect.
ext.popup.bridge_warning.back: This page's security settings block part of Undirect's protection.
ext.popup.bridge_warning.why: names this as a limitation of the one page, not a bug or a setting to fix

ext.kind.click_catcher.why: terse noun-phrase tag, reads naturally in a comma-joined list of kind tags

ext.kind.overlay.why: broader than the click-catcher tag: any see-through element, not specifically something clickable

ext.kind.synthetic_click.why: names a click the page's own script dispatched, not a real press

ext.kind.window_open.why: names a window the page opened through its own code

ext.kind.back_hijack.why: names a navigation fired right after the person's own back gesture

ext.kind.redirect.why: names the core same-tab-redirect hijack, kept short

ext.kind.pop_tab.why: names a tab-under-style new tab opened behind the press

ext.kind.network_rule.why: names the strongest, earliest kind of block, stopped before it reached the page

ext.reason.way_back.back: The address has a way back.
ext.reason.way_back.why: explains why the redirect was allowed: its own address carries a way back to the starting site

ext.reason.sized.back: The window opened at a set size.
ext.reason.sized.why: explains why the window was allowed: a deliberate size rather than a bare tab

ext.reason.took_press.why: explains the block in the fewest words the row's tight footnote budget allows

ext.reason.default_allow.why: explains the destination went through by the general default, not an explicit rule

ext.reason.own_code.back: The site itself opened the window.
ext.reason.own_code.why: explains the site's own code, not a third party, asked for the window

ext.popup.rules_link.why: one word, reused as the nav row, the screen's header title, and the back button's accessibility label

ext.popup.back_link.why: names the destination the chevron-only back button returns to (the popup's main per-site view), rather than the literal word 'back', matching how a VoiceOver label should name where it goes

ext.rules.everywhere_heading.why: reused consistently with the other 'everywhere' scope labels

ext.action.allow.why: infinitive menu action, scope already fixed by which section the row is in

ext.action.block.why: infinitive menu action, counterpart to Allow

ext.action.clear.why: same underlying action as app.rules.row.use_default, phrased identically for the tighter popup menu

ext.popup.settings_heading.why: the popup's own settings screen, reused as both the nav row and the header title

ext.settings.guard_label.why: kept identical to app.settings.guard_toggle for the same master switch, used both as the visible label and the sr-only switch label

ext.settings.guard_on.why: feminine form agreeing with 'Защита', specific to the guard switch's own state name

ext.settings.guard_off.why: feminine form agreeing with 'Защита', clear opposite of guard_on

ext.settings.mode_heading.why: kept identical to app.settings.mode_heading for the same setting

ext.settings.banner_toggle.why: kept the three-word phrase matching the app-side counterpart; Russian has no natural two-word way to say it, and it still fits a toggle row

ext.action.report.why: names opening a pre-filled report; nothing is sent automatically, matching the brief's note that the person still submits it themselves
